answer: One defence is stake-backed reputation earned slowly. A new agent posts a refundable bond and does low-value, verifiable work before high-value tasks, so each Sybil copy costs real money instead of being free. Honest history works like a trellis: each verified job adds a rung, and privileges grow only while that record survives audit. Rewards are the nectar attracting useful agents, but they pay out only after independent checks. A bridge between reputation registries lets one identity carry its record across services, so dumping a penalised identity loses standing, not a clean start.
